objective: Review git diff 2940cd3..2c6dfd0 (issue #22): (a) src/fetch/demo.ts, scripts/demo-result.ts and test/data/demo.test.ts record Demo.planned { at, late } from DEMO_PLANNED_AT / DEMO_STARTED_AT (late = started more than 30 min after planned; absent on manual runs; parseDemo keeps it on carry-over); (b) .github/workflows/demo.yml now ticks every 20 minutes ("4,24,44 * * * *") and a new `plan` job decides whether to record. Done when: (1) a scheduled tick records only once the DEMO_TIME (HH:MM, default 16:00) in DEMO_TZ (default America/Chicago) has passed, and at most once per day (it skips when snapshots/<today>.json on main already has demo.planned); (2) a run delayed past local midnight cannot file the video under the next day; (3) a manual run still records immediately and replaces that day's video, with no planned field; (4) the date used for the asset name and SNAPSHOT_DATE is the plan job's date; (5) a late start (> 30 min) is recorded as late:true; (6) bad DEMO_TIME/DEMO_TZ fail the run loudly (P-2); (7) a carried-over demo keeps planned, so later Snapshot runs the same day don't make the gate record again; (8) no secret or token is printed or committed (P-6); (9) every committed snapshot still parses. Specifically assess: (i) the concurrency group `demo` with cancel-in-progress false now covers the plan job too. Can two scheduled ticks both record on one day (a race between a recording run's commit and the next tick's gate)? Consider GitHub keeping only one pending run per group. (ii) The gate reads the snapshot through `gh api .../contents/...?ref=main` with `|| true`, so an API error is treated as 'no video yet'. Is that the right failure direction? (iii) Is `date -u -d 'TZ="America/Chicago" 2026-11-18 16:00'` correct GNU date syntax on ubuntu-latest, including across DST? (iv) 72 scheduled runs a day: any cost or quota issue for a public repo? Give severities blocking / major / minor.
